title: Normalization of compact-support system realization and Frobenius comparisons

source.place: Agent-formulated missing comparison prerequisite to clause (3), second paragraph: normalization of the whole finite-output system and the integral operation comparisons. The blueprint asserts the resulting transport realization, not this comparison theorem.

statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k_0$-schemes, supply a compactification $c_0$, and write $f=pj:X\to Y$ for its base change to $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use small pro-etale sites with $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $\mathscr S_W$ for strict semilinear $B_{W,n}$-module systems, $\mathcal R_W$ for simultaneous derived reduction, $U_W$ for exact levelwise restriction to $\widehat R_W$-module towers, and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim U_W$ [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put $F=S_pJ_j$ using total derived system direct image and exact open extension. For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], put
$$C_f(K)=F\mathcal R_XK,\qquad H_f(K)=\mathcal L_YC_f(K)=Rf_!^cK$$
with the last equality using [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The object $H_f(K)$ lies in $D^b_c(Y,R)$ by [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible]. Let $\mathcal T_f^c$ be the compact-support tower functor of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], with its specified quotient transitions.

There is a natural comparison isomorphism of whole towers
$$\delta_{f,K}:U_YC_f(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal T_f^c(K).$$
It is the comparison induced by the same simultaneous reduction, open extension, total derived proper direct image and scalar restriction models. It evaluates to the canonical identification with $\operatorname{Res}_nRf^c_{!,n}K_n$ and carries every transition to the quotient-induced transition followed by the coefficient-restriction comparison. Its derived-limit realization is the defining identification $\mathcal L_YC_f(K)=Rf_!^cK$, also on morphisms.

Here are the source and target normalizations for Frobenius exchange. For $W=X,\overline X,Y$, put $g_W=\operatorname{id}_{W_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], $G_{W,r}=(g_W^r)^{-1}$ on systems, and $P_{W,r}=L(g_W^r)^*$ on integral objects [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For $N\in D^b_c(W,R)$ the specified pullback/reduction map is a system isomorphism
$$b^W_{r,N}:\mathcal R_WP_{W,r}N\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{W,r}\mathcal R_WN.$$
For one flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to N$ it is the composite of two maps. The first is $\mathcal R_W(\kappa_N)^{-1}:\mathcal R_WP_{W,r}N\to\mathcal R_W(g_W^r)^{-1}N$, where $\kappa_N:(g_W^r)^{-1}N\to P_{W,r}N$ is the specified integral comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b), for $g=g_W^r$; its invertibility on this domain is part of the assertion. The target is computed on the flat-term K-flat representative $(g_W^r)^{-1}Q$. The second is the inverse of the tensor map $G_{W,r}(Q\otimes B_{W,n})\to(g_W^r)^{-1}Q\otimes B_{W,n}$, $G_{W,r}(x\otimes a)\mapsto G_{W,r}(x)\otimes c^{g_W^r}_{A_n}(G_{W,r}(a))$, of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-reduction-tower]. These are comparisons of the simultaneous quotient diagrams, with the coherent pullback-composition normalization of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Explicitly, writing $c^W_{m,N}:P_{W,1}P_{W,m}N\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{W,m+1}N$ and $t^W_m:G_{W,1}G_{W,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{W,m+1}$ for the inverse-direction compositors, one has the SYSTEM identity
$$\mathcal R_W(c^W_{m,N})\circ(b^W_{1,P_{W,m}N})^{-1}\circ G_{W,1}((b^W_{m,N})^{-1})=(b^W_{m+1,N})^{-1}\circ t^W_{m,\mathcal R_WN}.$$
Both sides map $G_{W,1}G_{W,m}\mathcal R_WN$ to $\mathcal R_WP_{W,m+1}N$. Set
$$v_{r,K}=F((b^X_{r,K})^{-1}):FG_{X,r}\mathcal R_XK\longrightarrow C_f(P_{X,r}K).$$
For a system $C$ over $Y$ with $\mathcal L_YC\in D^b_c(Y,R)$, let
$$\nu^Y_{r,C}:P_{Y,r}\mathcal L_YC\xrightarrow{\sim}(g_Y^r)^{-1}\mathcal L_YC\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_YG_{Y,r}C$$
be the inverse of the specified map $\kappa_{\mathcal L_YC}:(g_Y^r)^{-1}\mathcal L_YC\to P_{Y,r}\mathcal L_YC$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b), followed by exact inverse image commuting with the ENTIRE derived limit cone [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback, lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. The asserted comparison includes invertibility of that specified $\kappa$ on this domain. At $Y=s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ this is exactly the $\nu$ of [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-powers].

Under the defining identifications $H_f=\mathcal L_YC_f$, the canonical comparison maps $\alpha_{!,r},\beta_{!,r}$ used to define integral exchange in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], item 2, for the $r$-th-power square, satisfy the equalities
$$\alpha_{!,r,K}=\nu^Y_{r,C_f(K)}:P_{Y,r}H_f(K)\longrightarrow\mathcal L_YG_{Y,r}C_f(K),$$
$$\beta_{!,r,K}=\mathcal L_Y(v_{r,K}):\mathcal L_YFG_{X,r}\mathcal R_XK\longrightarrow H_f(P_{X,r}K).$$
These equalities use the total-limit cone and the actual simultaneous unit/counit constructions of the comparison maps; they hold as natural transformations, not merely after individual reductions. All the displayed identifications are natural in $K$ and compatible with the pullback compositors on $X$ and $Y$. The assertion holds for every bounded derived-complete constructible integral $K$, without a finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on its $A_n$-reductions. No comparison $\mathcal R_YH_f(K)\cong C_f(K)$ is assumed in this assertion.
